documents.text: Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position in Meta Platforms, arguing that alternative data from TickerTrends point to a significant slowdown in adoption of Muse, Meta’s flagship AI app, which CEO Mark Zuckerberg has highlighted as central to the company’s AI strategy. According to Hunterbrook Media’s report, weekly downloads fell 8.1% week over week to an average of approximately 165,000 per day during the seven days ended Oct. 7. Daily net additions of active users also declined sharply to around 74,000 in early October, down 62.4% from the average of 198,000 recorded in late September. Hunterbrook’s bearish thesis is that investor enthusiasm and Meta’s valuation gains may have outpaced the app’s actual operating performance. Beyond slowing user growth, the report identifies functional limitations, including access restrictions imposed by major third-party platforms such as Amazon, as well as increasing scrutiny over data privacy and security vulnerabilities. $META
